title: I used AI to translate my game into Spanish and Portuguese. I don't speak either. How do you actually check if the translations are good?
author: Critical-Truth-3404
selftext:
Hey everyone!

Someone requested Spanish in my game's feedback form, so I decided to add Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese using AI.

The problem is, I don't speak either language. 😂

I tried a few things to avoid blindly trusting the translations. I used a glossary to keep names consistent, got another AI to review everything, and wrote scripts to catch broken placeholders and other issues.

The second AI review actually caught some hilarious mistakes. One line translated to "a wife" instead of "handcuffed". So clearly, there's still room for improvement!

The translations are live now, but I have no idea how natural they sound to native speakers.

A few questions for developers here:

1. How do you usually check AI translations? Native speakers, paid proofreaders or something else?
2. Do players appreciate having their language available even if the translation isn't perfect?
3. Any tips for making dialogue and slang sound natural?

If you speak Spanish or Portuguese and want to check it out, here's the game:

[https://warlordvii.itch.io/found-by-dusk](https://warlordvii.itch.io/found-by-dusk)

You can press B in-game to send feedback with a screenshot. If you leave your name, I'll add you to the credits!

Thanks!

comments.author: Briskfall
comments.body:
Translators have their own AI pipelines but that's their moat.

It's not easy and requires multiple passes to get a good one working. If you have a second language that you're good at working with it would work well as a good foundation.

Like, I have 3 languages that I would say that I'm okay at, and 2 of them that I'm only at a learner's level. I tried to build a translation pipeline for the ones I'm able in and it was very tokens intensive and required plenty of trials and errors to keep things consistent with the original tone. LLMs have a bad habit of using approximates that can change the characterization and intent of your character, and tailored prompts would solve that. I wouldn't trust myself at all with the 2 languages that I'm only an amateur at, much less with languages I have zero foundation in, lol.

Also, the model choice is important too. I would not trust my life for translations if it's a small model, or ones that's been distilled.

I would say that it should cut you development time if you were to find translators supercharged with LLMs, instead of undertaking it all on your own. You'd be flinging back and forth with plenty of passes with no end in sight.

The complexity exists because it encompasses a hidden challenge: it is as much of a writing problem more than a translation one.
